sense: the natural world, as against what people make

terms.gloss: nature: the world as it is made, not built by people
evidence: Varr. RR 3.1.4: dīvīna nātūra dedit agrōs, ars hūmāna aedificāvit urbēs
terms.comment: Nature as the maker and order of things, set against human skill (ars): sīc nātūra sōlitārium nihil amat (Cic. Amic. 88). For “I love nature” Morgan–Owens suggests juvat rūsticārī or libenter in silvīs ac campīs versor (see countryside).

terms.gloss: nature as a whole, the physical world
terms.grammar: noun, first declension, with a genitive
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.154: in perspiciendā cognōscendāque rērum nātūrā
terms.comment: Lucretius’s and Cicero’s phrase for the whole of nature, the subject of natural science. Morgan–Owens takes it, with a query, from Egger for the natural world as against what people make.

Egger’s coinage for “the environment”, which Morgan–Owens marks as doubtful. Classically ambitus is a circuit, the space left round a house, and above all illegal canvassing for votes (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: dīvīna nātūra dedit agrōs, ars hūmāna aedificāvit urbēs
phrases.english: divine nature gave us the fields, human skill built the cities

phrases.latin: nec sōlem proprium nātūra nec āera fēcit nec tenuēs undās: ad pūblica mūnera vēnī
phrases.english: nature made neither the sun nor the air nor clear water anyone’s own: I have come to a gift that belongs to all

sources: Lewis & Short: natura · Lewis & Short: res · Lewis & Short: ambitus
